name: SikaPlast-300 E
paste:
SIKAPLAST®-300 E: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaPlast®-300 E, June 2024, Version 01.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/t/sikaplast-300-e.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaPlast®-300 E where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (June 2024, Version 01.01).
1.2 Product description. SikaPlast®-300 E has been designed to provide both water reduction and excellent slump-keeping properties. SikaPlast®-300 E improves the rheology and pumpability of concrete produced using manufactured sand.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. SikaPlast®-300 E is used for:
    - Production of pre-mixed concrete to facilitate improved strengths, durability or economy.
    - Long-distance concrete delivery.
    - Production of concrete for use in extended pumping or placing operations.
    - Production of concrete made with manufactured orpoorly-shaped natural sands.
    - Piling mixtures.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaPlast®-300 E
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Mid-range water reducing admixture with superior slump retention
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (June 2024, Version 01.01) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Water reduction, leading to improved strength and durability of the hardened concrete.
    - Significant improvement in the slump-keeping ability of fresh concrete. This reduces the risk of rejected loads due to premature slump loss and maintains concrete workability for extended pumping or placing requirements.
    - Improvement in pumpability of concrete made using manufactured sand.
    - Facilitates an increase in the percentage of manufactured or poor-quality natural sand in the concrete.
    - Delivers softer concrete.
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: SikaPlast®-300 E is an aqueous solution of selected modified polycarboxylates.
    - Appearance and colour: Clear liquid.
    - Density: 1.04 kg/l approximately.
2.5 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: Bulk deliveries; 1000 litre IBC
    - Shelf life: Stored at temperature between 5°C and 35°C, in unopened original containers protected from direct sunlight and frost, shelf life is 12 months.
    - Storage conditions: Store SikaPlast®-300 E at temperature between 5°C and 35 °C, protected from direct sunlight.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (June 2024, Version 01.01) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (June 2024, Version 01.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Dispensing: SikaPlast®-300 E should be added with the initial batch water. Never add to dry mix. For best results we recommend thorough mixing of the wet concrete for at least 60 seconds per cubic metre.
    - Compatibility: SikaPlast®-300 E is compatible with all Sika concrete admixtures, except for Sikament® NN.
4.3 Recommended dosage. Typical dosage for general concrete production is between 300 to 800 ml/100 kg of total binder content. Optimum dosage depends on site conditions,mix ingredients, and desired plastic and hardened concrete properties. Laboratory and field trials shall be conducted to determine the required dosage of SikaPlast®-300 E.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (June 2024, Version 01.01) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.4 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaPlast®-300 E, June 2024, Version 01.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/t/sikaplast-300-e.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaPlast®-300 E, version 29/05/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/r/sds-sikaplast-300e.pdf
    - Environmental Product Declaration: EPD SikaPlast®-300 E, version 12/11/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/1/epd-sikaplast-300e.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
